findings.message: Base-case cap rate of 3.63% independently verified (NOI $6,780 / $187,000). Well below the 10% threshold; REJECTED classification is supported.
High-rent scenario ($1,000/mo, evidence range_high) yields 4.91% cap rate—still far below 10%. Low-rent scenario ($650/mo) yields 2.66%. No plausible rent within documented comps supports VIABLE.

Rent ESTIMATED MEDIUM at $800/mo with documented comp range $650–$1,000. Base estimate is mid-range and not overly optimistic, but price-to-rent ratio ($187k / $800/mo ≈ 19.4×) is incompatible with a 10% unlevered cap rate at realistic expense loads.

HOA alicuota is ESTIMATED LOW at $80/mo pending condominium confirmation. Evidence cites the listing but does not verify the alicuota amount. Higher HOA would further compress an already sub-threshold cap rate; does not change REJECTED outcome.

Special assessments UNKNOWN (LOW confidence). Underwriting correctly excludes them from the base expense total rather than assuming zero. Any confirmed assessment would reduce NOI further; does not change REJECTED outcome.

Rental and STR restrictions both UNKNOWN (LOW confidence). LTR-only income path is assumed without bylaws or HOA rental policy. Restrictions could limit achievable rent or use case but are immaterial given cap rate gap.
Purchase price VERIFIED HIGH at $187,000 via YapaTree listing. Price anchor is well supported.

Underwriter cites ~$2,018/mo rent needed for 10% cap; independent check at fixed $2,820/yr expenses yields ~$1,793/mo (($18,700 NOI + $2,820) / 12). Either figure exceeds evidence range_high ($1,000/mo) by a wide margin.
Taxes ESTIMATED LOW at $50/yr per Ecuador predial norms. Even a materially higher tax bill would not close the gap to 10% cap rate.
